rules: Workers never edit this file. Only the orchestrator accepts a non-bootstrap feature using accept-feature.sh after a matching passing VerificationRecord exists, recording accepted_run_id, accepted_verification_sha256, accepted_at, and accepted_by with passes:true. Editing or removing approved descriptions/steps is unacceptable. Keep bootstrap on every feature: false (default) requires verified worker execution and separate acceptance; true exempts work no worker will ever run, such as mission scaffolding or orchestrator decisions. Set it when authoring; never add it after GATE 0 to excuse missing evidence.

features.description: Provider, door and pool registry as manifest-owned data (harness-registry.json), replacing PROVIDERS, CAPABILITIES and SEAT_SPECS. FALLBACKS is copied into the registry unchanged for parity and deleted in F004. Per provider: probe command, list parser, identity check (--version), effort and fast encoding (flag or model name), discovery directory. Per door: billing class, pool, no-ZDR flag, priority. Naming rule: the provider name is `cursor` (binary `cursor-agent`); `agent` stays only as a legacy name so v3 evidence still validates. Also scripts/fleet-doctor.sh: for each provider it resolves every PATH hit to its real binary, checks identity with --version, and checks login with a tiny probe. ERROR only for two different binaries with one name, wrong identity, or logged out. Duplicate PATH entries and symlinks are WARN. mission-init and dispatch run the doctor instead of ad-hoc `which -a` checks.
steps: harness-registry.json is valid JSON and is listed in harness-manifest.json ownership

A parity test shows the registry yields the same providers, capabilities, seat specs and fallbacks as the old constants; after the switch `grep -nE '^(PROVIDERS|CAPABILITIES|SEAT_SPECS) *= *[({]' scripts/*.py` exits 1 (names may remain as loaded values; literal definitions may not; FALLBACKS stays until F004)
The test fails when any provider lacks probe, list parser, identity check, effort/fast encoding or discovery directory, or any door lacks billing class, pool, no-ZDR flag or priority
Provider `cursor` has binary `cursor-agent`; `agent` appears only as a legacy name; v3 evidence that names `agent` still validates
fleet-doctor.sh exits 0 on this Mac and prints WARN (not ERROR) for the duplicate PATH entries (local-only check: a task verification command, never part of tests/run-tests.sh or CI)
fleet-doctor.sh fixtures exit non-zero with ERROR for: two different binaries sharing a name, a wrong --version identity, a logged-out probe

`grep -l fleet-doctor.sh .agents/skills/mission-init/SKILL.md .agents/skills/dispatch-worker/SKILL.md` lists both files, and `grep -nE 'which -a|command -v agent' .agents/skills/mission-init/SKILL.md .agents/skills/dispatch-worker/SKILL.md` exits 1
shellcheck scripts/*.sh tests/*.sh and bash tests/run-tests.sh exit 0

features.description: Observed model, usage and fast state in receipts, from each CLI's JSON output. Unknown stays `unknown`.
steps: A receipt schema test requires observed_model, usage (input, output, cache, reasoning) and fast_state, each with a source flag observed|estimated|unknown

Fixture outputs for claude, codex, cursor-agent and agy fill the fields; a CLI that reports nothing gives `unknown`; the cursor-agent fixture (usage and session_id, no model) gives observed_model `unknown` unless the stream-json init event reports the model
An old receipt without the new fields still validates
No code path writes a guessed value as `observed`
shellcheck and bash tests/run-tests.sh exit 0

features.description: Fleet v2: policy seats, per-spawn resolution recorded in the spec, drift events, door priority, fast and credits opt-in. Cursor and Antigravity effort through the model name. Resolves the unproven `model[effort=…,fast=…]` format. Needs Gate 0 decision 2 (frozen-fleet amendment).
steps: A fleet v2 seat names a family and a policy; a v1 fleet.json still validates
Each spawn records the resolved model in the spec and the observed model in the receipt
A fixture with a model change between two runs writes exactly one drift event to the drift log; a test shows the spawn exits non-zero if the drift event cannot be written
Door priority picks the first included, healthy door; a credits or api door is skipped unless the mission approves it
A `-fast` model is never chosen unless the mission enables fast
Cursor and agy effort is encoded in the model name from the registry; a test lists the encoding for each
The unproven `model[effort=…,fast=…]` format is either proven by a recorded probe or removed; no unproven format ships
The FALLBACKS constant is deleted from scripts/fleet_state.py (`grep -nE '^FALLBACKS *= *[({]' scripts/*.py` exits 1); an unavailable family stays `unavailable`, never a guessed model
shellcheck and bash tests/run-tests.sh exit 0

features.description: Ledger v1: schema, writer in the runner, privacy rule, derived-view helper.
steps: A schema file defines every row field named in proposal section 8, with a source flag on every number
The runner writes one valid row per run, including failed runs, to `.tasks/ledger/<run_id>.json` (gitignored); a test shows this write never dirties the Git tree
A test fails if a row contains transcript text, prompt text or a secret-like string
The derived-view helper prints first-try rate and tokens per accepted feature from fixture rows; it stores nothing
.tasks/logs/ is gitignored and a test shows no log file is staged

A fold command appends the rows from `.tasks/ledger/` to docs/missions/ledger.jsonl exactly once per run id (a second run of the command adds nothing); an integration test shows the runner write keeps the next launch's clean-tree check and verify-mission.sh snapshot check passing, and the fold lands in the orchestrator's acceptance commit
shellcheck and bash tests/run-tests.sh exit 0

features.description: Structured verdicts: JSON schemas for the Architect's task plan and review, validated for any provider (`--json-schema` where the CLI has it).
steps: A task-plan schema and a review schema exist and are valid JSON Schema
A validator script exits 0 on a good fixture and non-zero on each bad fixture (missing field, wrong type, empty steps)
The registry records per provider whether the CLI supports --json-schema; where it does not, the validator checks the output after the run
mission-init and the review action name the schemas
shellcheck and bash tests/run-tests.sh exit 0

features.description: Real smoke on the Mac: one small mission through 4 doors and 5 runs: `claude`, `codex`, `cursor-agent` (Composer and Grok) and `agy`, with ledger rows and reconstructable evidence.
steps: A smoke mission exists with one tiny task per run: claude, codex, cursor-agent with Composer, cursor-agent with Grok, and agy
Five receipts exist under .tasks/receipts/, one per run; each has a non-unknown observed model, except cursor-agent runs may stay `unknown` when the CLI does not report the model
Five ledger rows exist, one per receipt, and each validates against the ledger schema
bash scripts/verify-mission.sh exits 0 for the smoke mission
A reconstruct command prints, per smoke run id, its spec, receipt, VerificationRecord and ledger row, and exits non-zero if any of the four is missing; the human reads that output at Gate 2
